Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

School & learning

times table noun

also times tables, multiplication table, tables, twice two

our formation

tabula multiplicātiōnis

a times table

Our plain description, since none of the works consulted names it: multiplicātiō is multiplication in Columella (5.2.1, Lewis & Short), and a tabula any written list.

Other words

  • bis bīna — twice two: the table as it is said

    also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 2.49; Varr. RR 2.1.12: ter ternās, three times three (Lewis & Short, s.v. ternī)

    Latin says the table with a numeral adverb and a distributive: bis bīna quattuor, ter terna novem. Cicero’s Balbus says that Epicurus had not even learned what twice two makes (N. D. 2.49).

Examples

  • quae sī bis bīna quot essent didicisset Epicūrus, certē nōn dīceret

    if Epicurus had learned what twice two makes, he would certainly not say thisCic. N. D. 2.49

  • jam vērō ūnum et ūnum duo, duo et duo quattuor, odiōsa cantiō mihi erat

    and ‘one and one is two, two and two is four’ was a hateful chant to meAug. Conf. 1.13.22

  • Ter terna quot sunt? — Novem.

    What are three threes? — Nine.composed

See also multiply, arithmetic, learn by heart, sum.
